pairs.difference: A: the envelope is tilted, with the photos fanned and overlapping out of its mouth. It reads as a thin stack, and its 0.855 planar share is above the real range, but that fits a nearly flat object and the view holds together. B: the bat is square-on, with both wings spread flat in the picture plane and no wing receding. The body is a smooth rainbow ball pasted on those flat wings. Real floating heroes are usually turned at an angle.
pairs.fix: Turn the bat three-quarters so the near wing comes forward and looks larger and the far wing recedes and looks shorter. Show the body from the same angle as the wings.

pairs.difference: A: the cauldron's rim is open enough to show the brew from above, but the legs and belly sit close to eye level. The rock slab has its own broad top and a craggy front cut off by the bottom edge, so it reads as a stage at a different tilt. B: the sneakers share one raised three-quarter view, parallel to each other, on a simple floor with a clean horizon.
pairs.fix: Use one camera height for the whole cauldron: rim ellipse, legs and rock top should match. Replace the craggy slab with a simple flat surface with a thin edge.

pairs.difference: Both planar shares are below the real range, so the number does not separate them. A: the topiary stands on a thin curb ring with lawn, path, hedge and sky behind, and the ground stays at one angle. B: the pumpkins stack up in many layers: big foreground tufts, pumpkins and vines, fence, hills, distant trees and clouds. The background is as sharp as the hero, like the extra scene depth added on the generated lighthouses.
pairs.fix: Keep only ground, hero and one soft simple backdrop. Remove the fence, hills and distant trees, or reduce them to a blurred band of color.

pairs.difference: A: a low camera looks up at the capital, whose left volute swings round in a strong forced turn. The wall lines angle steeply, yet the plinth top is seen from above, and the plaque sits at its own tilt. The column does not share one view. B: the suitcase is nearly frontal with one level floor, planks converging gently, mild perspective and no competing views.
pairs.fix: Use a mild three-quarter view at chest height. Keep the column upright with level top and base ellipses, the wall lines nearly horizontal, and the plaque turned to the same angle as the plinth.

pairs.difference: A: the headstone's front is one nearly flat facing slab, leaning to the side, with a thick edge only on the right. It sits on a low mound seen from near ground level, so the stone's turn and the ground do not clearly agree. B: the slide, platform and pool deck read as one raised three-quarter view, with the underside of the platform and the top of the deck both consistent with a camera at mid height.
pairs.fix: Turn the headstone clearly three-quarters with an even thickness along one side, and show its base sunk into a ground plane seen from the same height.

pairs.difference: A: the mower has a coherent three-quarter view from above, with wheel ellipses that agree with each other and with the grass. B: the broom stands balanced at a steep lean with the handle running up flat and no foreshortening. The planks fan strongly to a vanishing point below a low wall line, so the floor has stronger perspective than the broom on it.
pairs.fix: Lean the broom against a wall or show it from one mild angle, with the far end of the handle slightly smaller. Make the floor planks converge only gently.

pairs.difference: A: a low worm's-eye camera makes the house flare and lean, with verticals spreading and roofs bending, while the hill and steps are seen from a different height. The perspective is forced and warped, though the crookedness may be partly design. B: the door is square-on and even, with panels staying parallel and the leaves overlapping as a simple foreground frame.
pairs.fix: Lower the perspective strength. Show the house from a gentle three-quarter view with verticals nearly parallel, and with the steps, windows and roof edges all following one eye level.

pairs.difference: A: the pumpkin is nearly front-on and floating, its face laid across the swollen rainbow ball with only a thin rim of cut depth, and the stem gives the only hint of turn. B: the jacket is turned, with the sleeves receding and the cuff openings and collar interior giving real overlap and depth, though the cuffs lean slightly toward a lower view than the collar.
pairs.fix: Turn the pumpkin a clear three-quarter away from the viewer so the face wraps around the curve, and show thick cut walls on the far side of each eye and mouth opening.

pairs.difference: A: the crystal ball is front-on above a dead-level table band. The stand's ring is open as if seen from above, but all the feet sit on one straight line, so they show no depth on the table top. The 0.718 planar share, above the real range, comes from the wall and table bands. B: the vending machine is turned with its left side visible, gentle convergence and a soft floor glow blended into the wall.
pairs.fix: Raise the camera slightly and show more table top, with the front foot of the stand lower than the two back feet so the base matches the ring's ellipse.

pairs.difference: A: the coffin is seen from high up with a huge lid, and its near end swells while it tapers hard to the far end, giving wide-angle convergence. The flagstones and level striped wall behind suggest a lower, calmer camera, so hero and floor disagree. The 0.711 planar share is above the real range. B: the rocking chair has one coherent three-quarter view, with rockers, seat and back agreeing and the planks receding to a level wall line.
pairs.fix: Lower the camera and weaken the perspective so the near and far ends of the coffin are closer in size. Match the angle of the floor stones to the lid and side.

pairs.difference: A: the candelabra is dead-frontal and symmetrical, floating with no ground. The base shows a dark open underside ellipse as if seen from below, yet the arms lie flat in the picture plane and do not come forward. B: the lamp post also has a low camera and a cropped base, but the dome, ring collars and bowl all share that one view from below, and the bottom crop anchors it.
pairs.fix: Turn the candelabra slightly so one arm comes toward the viewer and the other recedes. Show the top of the base as a filled solid ellipse, not a hollow underside.

pairs.difference: A: the balloons are simple round forms with clear overlap against a soft, simpler cloud layer, and all share one view. B: the masts and spars lean in different directions, and the hull is seen from above into the deck while the water has a low horizon and flat sea. Sails, hull and sea do not share a single camera.
pairs.fix: Use one three-quarter camera for the whole ship: masts parallel, spars at matching angles, and deck tilt matching the height of the sea horizon.

pattern: Generated cards rarely fail on any one form. They give themselves away when the parts stop sharing one camera. The rim, base, ground and props are each drawn from their own height, as with the cauldron and rock slab, the column and plaque, and the ship. Perspective is also pushed too hard, as with the coffin's near-end swell, the house's flaring verticals and the broom's fanning planks. Floating heroes tend to sit square-on and flat, like the bat, pumpkin and candelabra, where real ones are turned with one part clearly receding. Backgrounds gain extra sharp layers of scenery, where real cards keep ground, hero and a simple backdrop. planar_share only helps at the extremes, and it reflects flat walls and flat objects as much as the camera.
